newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen steady - private.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen steady - private.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hogs were expected to trade steady on Wednesday amid outlooks for increased hog movement as temperatures moderate in the Corn Belt, livestock dealers and packer buyers said.
Extreme heat and humidity reportedly had kept some farmers from risking sorting and shipping hogs because of increased stress on the animals early this week, sources said.
Temperatures moderated in the western belt on Tuesday, but remained hot and sticky in the east, the dealers said.
"Looks like we're going to have a few more hogs," one Indiana dealer said of an expected pickup in marketings Wednesday as temperatures there recede.

Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota top prices for hogs delivered to plant were seen at $61.00, sources there said. Prices there on Tuesday closed at $61.00, up $1.50 from Monday and up $3.00 from Friday, USDA confirmed.
Illinois top hog prices at plants were seen unchanged at $60.50 and Indiana/Ohio hogs at plants were seen at $61.50, sources in those areas said.
